correctness.rationale: The odd-mex generating function follows from the forced-presence and absent-size factors; modulo \(8\) all mex classes \(j\geq2\) vanish. The \(j=1\) class contributes \(4q^3/((1-q)(1-q^2))\). Jacobi triple product gives \(P(q)=(1+2\Theta(q))^{-1}\), whose exact modulo-eight expansion is \(1-2\Theta(q)+4\Theta(q)^2\); in characteristic two, \(\Theta(q)^2\) has support at twice squares. Convolution with \(q/(1+q)\) yields \((-1)^{n-1}\lfloor\sqrt{n-1}\rfloor\), and the rational correction has coefficient \(\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor\). Square-index parity gives zero modulo eight for every positive square; nonsquares have residues two or six. Counting residues in the two-step square gaps proves the asymptotic half-densities. The embedded checker reconstructs all coefficients modulo eight through \(n=400\) and independently enumerates weighted ordinary partitions through \(n=24\); these finite computations corroborate but do not replace the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The exact generating function and a modulo-four square criterion in arXiv:2609.32207v1 are acknowledged. Its eight main theorem statements include no coefficientwise closed modulo-eight residue law for the odd-valued ordinary mex statistic and no density-one-half classification; its modulo-eight theorem instead treats self-convolution. The published exact generating function determines every coefficient in principle, so this is a new arithmetic extraction of an existing generating series, not discovery of the series. Relevant prior published-finding corpus records concern distinct objects. An equivalent derivation in unindexed literature or unseen material of a related 2026 preprint remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: An equivalent closed formula may appear in unindexed recent literature.

The new arithmetic consequence can be derived from the already-published exact generating function; novelty is in the explicit congruence, cancellation pattern and distribution, not in the series identity.

value.rationale: The full direct modulo-eight distribution of a recently introduced overpartition odd-mex statistic closes a motivated arithmetic gap beyond the published modulo-four square-support theorem. Its exact square zero locus persists under doubled modulus; all nonsquares split into residues 2 and 6 according to an explicit square-root/twice-square arithmetic rule, and each nonzero residue has density 1/2. This is a natural complete coefficient classification, not an arbitrary finite slice or unmotivated computation. It does not claim valuations beyond the modulus-eight threshold.
